NFC Authenticator Privacy Policy

Effective: October 27, 2026
Developer: Lukas Voegtle

Overview

The developer operates no authentication backend and receives no registration or authentication data. The app has no advertising, analytics, or tracking SDK. Transfers occur only when the user presents the phone to an NFC service.

Data stored locally

For each approved service and authentication profile, the app stores the service domain and disclosure metadata, approved fields and purposes, policy and deletion links, key fingerprints, approval time, an opaque service-issued credential reference, an optional alias, and profile-specific credentials. Signing keys are not reused across services or profiles. Authentication attempts are kept only in memory.

Transfers

Before registration, the app shows the recipient, operator, certificate-verified domain, exact requested fields and purposes, policy and deletion links, authentication profile, and encryption identity. Registration requires “Agree and register.” Identifying and authentication payloads are end-to-end encrypted directly to the selected service. The developer and intermediaries cannot decrypt them, and no undisclosed field is sent. A limited HTTPS request checks that the service policy is accessible.

Independent services

Each recipient controls subsequent processing under its own policy. Domain-certificate verification proves control of the service domain; it does not certify the named operator or legal sufficiency of its policy.

Retention and deletion

Local registrations remain until deleted in the app, app storage is cleared, or the app is uninstalled. Android backup is disabled. Local deletion removes the record, profile-specific signing key, and credential keys, but not the service’s copy; use its displayed deletion instructions.

Security and logs

Private signing keys are held by Android Keystore and stored credential secrets are encrypted locally. The app accepts only protocol version 3 encrypted traffic. Logs do not contain names, identifiers, keys, plaintext, or decrypted registration/authentication data.

Contact

App privacy requests: https://github.com/voegtlel/nfcauth/issues. Service data requests must use that service’s deletion contact.

Published policy: https://voegtlel.github.io/nfcauth/privacy-policy.html
